subsystem.name: MathAndCollision
subsystem.responsibility: Low-level geometry helpers and the resource containers that own them: in-place 3x3 matrix rotation with Euler extraction, a nine-bucket object hash table with chain traversal and per-bucket release, a display-mode list built from the sound manager, and teardown/reset helpers for multi-array resource owners.

summary: This scope is a mixture of math utility and resource lifecycle code. AngleAxisRotateMatrixToEuler (0x00567120) applies a Rodrigues angle-axis rotation to an in-place 3x3 float matrix and extracts Euler angles, skipping the rotation when the axis magnitude is zero or non-finite. ObjectIDLookupAcross9Arrays (0x005684A0) and NinePointerArrayCleanup (0x00567F10) share a receiver shaped as nine dword slots: the first resolves a name to a hash entry and walks each bucket chain, the second releases every non-null slot pointer and nulls the slot. DisplayModeArrayAllocFromSoundManager (0x0055BE80) and freePointerArrayWithLinkedListCleanup (0x0055BF70) both operate on a list object with a count at +0x04 and a pointer array at +0x08; one builds 292-byte DisplayMode structs from sound-manager entries and the other frees them. ResourceTeardownWithStateArrayReset (0x00558990) releases two audio sub-resources (object at sub-context+0x1C, drain at sub-context+0x24) and resets a 128-byte-stride state array. ResetAndFreeMemberArrays (0x0056E970) tears down an owner holding four counted arrays (580/48/48/72-byte elements) plus three optional pointers and a trailing four-pointer block. No receiver class identity is proven for any function; all owners are labeled UnknownObject in the source packet and every class here is a DERIVED/GUESS grouping of shared offset patterns.

function_roles.role: teardown - release audio sub-resources (reset+free object at this+0x6C via ObjectResetWithVirtualRelease, finalize+free drain at this+0x74 via DrainingLoopFinalizer), clear flag bit 0x100 at this+0x20, reset every 128-byte state-struct element and zero the counters

build - allocate a 292-byte DisplayMode struct per sound-manager entry, copy the entry name, record the index, register the struct and append it to the slot array; invoked from RenderUISystemGlobalInit; on zero-init failure free the partial struct

teardown - iterate the count of pointer slots at this+0x8, free each slot's linked list via LinkedListFreeWithTraversalAndNulling, free each non-null slot pointer, and null the slot; returns the count

math - apply an angle-axis (Rodrigues) rotation in place to the 3x3 float matrix this, skipping the rotation when the axis squared-magnitude is zero or non-finite (FPU status 0x4100), then always extract Euler angles into the a3 output buffer
teardown - iterate the nine dword slots of the receiver, call sub_567CC0 on each non-null slot pointer, then null the slot; returns the last processed slot's result

lookup - resolve a name string to a hash-table entry index via HashTableEntrySearch, then walk the nine buckets and their node chains (ShortComputation_adb0 / SimpleFieldGetter_bfc0), calling sub_568320 on every node whose FieldGetter_79d0 equals the index; returns the found flag

teardown - free four counted arrays (580-byte elements with per-element destructor at 0x00568E60; 48/48/72-byte pointer-element arrays) and the three optional pointers, clear all slots, then free the trailing four-pointer block at this+0x34

classes.name: ResourceTeardownOwner
classes.responsibility: Receiver of ResourceTeardownWithStateArrayReset. Holds a flags dword, a sub-context at +0x50 containing an audio object pointer (+0x1C inside the sub-context, absolute this+0x6C) and a drain pointer (+0x24 inside the sub-context, absolute this+0x74), plus a 128-byte-stride state-struct array at +0x34 with a count at +0x2C and two counters at +0x30/+0x38.

classes.name: DisplayModeList
classes.responsibility: Container for DisplayMode structs built from the sound manager. Count/counter dword at +0x00, count at +0x04, pointer array of DisplayMode slots at +0x08. Build path (0x0055BE80) allocates and registers 292-byte structs; teardown path (0x0055BF70) frees each slot's linked list and the slot pointer.

classes.name: DisplayMode
classes.responsibility: 292-byte display-mode descriptor allocated and populated by DisplayModeArrayAllocFromSoundManager: index written at +0x00, name string copied at +0x04 from the sound-manager entry at entry+24 (evidence only via callee refs), index mirror at +0x104 and two zero-initialized dwords at +0x108 and +0x10C. Partially zero-initialized by PartialStructZeroInit and registered by DisplayModeEnumeratorWrapper. Only the +0x104/+0x108/+0x10C fields carry field evidence refs in this packet; the +0x00/+0x04 layout is from operation text.

classes.name: RotationMatrixMath
classes.responsibility: Receiver of AngleAxisRotateMatrixToEuler: an in-place row-major 3x3 float matrix (this[0..8], floats at +0x00..+0x20). Applies Rodrigues angle-axis rotation when the axis squared-magnitude is finite and non-zero, then always extracts Euler angles into the output buffer; gimbal lock handled at |this[5]| == 1.0.

classes.name: NineBucketTable
classes.responsibility: Receiver shared by ObjectIDLookupAcross9Arrays and NinePointerArrayCleanup: nine dword slots acting as linked-list bucket heads at +0x00..+0x20. The lookup resolves a name to a hash index and walks each bucket's chain (advancing via ShortComputation_adb0 / SimpleFieldGetter_bfc0, comparing FieldGetter_79d0); the cleanup releases each non-null slot pointer via sub_567CC0 and nulls it.

classes.name: MultiArrayOwner
classes.responsibility: Receiver of ResetAndFreeMemberArrays: four counted arrays anchored at +0x04 (580-byte elements), +0x0C (48-byte pointer elements), +0x14 (48-byte pointer elements) and +0x1C (72-byte pointer elements), each with a count in the header at array-4 and an owner slot at the even offsets; three optional pointers at +0x24/+0x28/+0x2C and a trailing four-pointer block at +0x34.

interfaces.name: AllocatorContract
interfaces.purpose: Allocation/deallocation contract used across the scope: OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper (0x00587C03) allocates blocks (e.g. 292-byte DisplayMode structs), FreeWrapper_7bcf (0x00587BCF) releases them. DisplayModeList build/teardown, ResourceTeardownOwner and MultiArrayOwner all rely on the free half.

interfaces.name: BucketChainTraversal
interfaces.purpose: Node-chain walk contract for the NineBucketTable lookup: advance to the next node via ShortComputation_adb0 (0x0049ADB0) and SimpleFieldGetter_bfc0 (0x0055BFC0), and read the per-node discriminator field via FieldGetter_79d0 (0x004979D0) to compare against the resolved hash index.

interfaces.name: SoundManager
interfaces.purpose: GUESS singleton reached through global handle dword_8B78A0. Prepared with a configuration argument via 0x0053D970, exposes an entry count via 0x0053D880 and a per-entry accessor via 0x0053D890 returning the entry whose +24 offset is a name string. Consumed by DisplayModeList build. Concrete type unproven; these three callees cannot be class methods here because none is a packet function.

compatibility_contracts.name: DisplayModeListLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: DisplayModeList: count/counter dword at +0x00, count at +0x04, DisplayMode pointer array at +0x08. Each DisplayMode is a 292-byte block: index at +0x00, name string at +0x04, index mirror at +0x104, two dwords zero-initialized at +0x108/+0x10C. A replacement display-mode registry must preserve this layout for the build and teardown paths.

compatibility_contracts.name: SoundManagerEntryEnumeration
compatibility_contracts.description: GUESS: global sound-manager handle 0x008B78A0 is prepared with a configuration argument via 0x0053D970, exposes an entry count via 0x0053D880 and a per-entry accessor via 0x0053D890 whose result holds the name string at +24. DisplayMode construction depends on this enumeration; a replacement must reproduce it if display-mode building is retained.

compatibility_contracts.name: AudioSubResourceTeardown
compatibility_contracts.description: Teardown must reset+free the audio object at sub-context+0x1C (absolute this+0x6C) via ObjectResetWithVirtualRelease with global 0x008B78A0, finalize+free the drain at sub-context+0x24 (absolute this+0x74) via DrainingLoopFinalizer, free both when still non-null, zero both pointers, and clear flag bit 0x100 at this+0x20.

compatibility_contracts.name: StateArrayReset
compatibility_contracts.description: State-struct array at this+0x34 with 128-byte stride and element count at this+0x2C. Reset clears header bit 6 of each element and zeroes element fields at +0x78 and +0x7C (absolute this+0xAC and this+0xB0 for element 0), then zeroes the counters at this+0x30 and this+0x38.

compatibility_contracts.name: EulerRotationMatrixLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: Rotation helper operates on an in-place row-major 3x3 float matrix (this[0..8] at +0x00..+0x20). The Rodrigues step is skipped when the axis squared-magnitude is zero or non-finite (FPU status mask 0x4100). Euler extraction must handle gimbal lock at fabs(this[5]) == 1.0.

unresolved: No receiver class identity is proven for any function; every owner is labeled UnknownObject in the source packet and the class names here are synthetic groupings of shared offset patterns.

dword_8B78A0 is treated as a sound-manager handle but its concrete type is not proven; the same global is passed to ObjectResetWithVirtualRelease and DrainingLoopFinalizer, whose role as first argument is unexplained.
Nature of the sub-context at this+0x50 (holding the audio object and drain pointers) and its owner class are unknown.
State-struct array element layout beyond the 128-byte stride is unknown, including the meaning of header bit 6.
Why flag bit 8 at this+0x20 is cleared only when the audio sub-resources existed is unclear.
Purpose of the unused second argument (a2/a3) of DisplayModeArrayAllocFromSoundManager is unknown.
Relationship between the this[1] tail counter and the slot array at this+0x8 is unverified.
DisplayMode layout at +0x00 (index) and +0x04 (name) is supported only by operation text, not by a field evidence ref, so no field entries could be produced for them.
EmptyStub_7470 (0x00557470) is described as a no-op stub; its actual behavior is not evidenced in this packet.
The per-slot linked lists freed by LinkedListFreeWithTraversalAndNulling (0x0055BBA0) are not reconciled with the 292-byte DisplayMode struct contents.

Globals dbl_59E420, flt_59E43C, flt_59E440 and flt_59E670 are read by AngleAxisRotateMatrixToEuler per the fact table but do not appear in the decompiled text; they may back the FPU-status (0x4100) or threshold comparisons.
Exact Euler extraction output-slot ordering (which angle maps to a3[0], a3[1], a3[2]) is inferred from matrix element reads, not evidenced by names.

Matrix element this[7] (offset 0x1C) is read during the rotation loop but has no dedicated field evidence ref in the packet; it is listed on RotationMatrixMath with only source:raw alongside the general field ref.
Semantics of sub_567CC0 (per-bucket release) and sub_568320 (action on a matching node) are unknown from this packet.

The two FieldGetter_79d0 comparisons in ObjectIDLookupAcross9Arrays pass uninitialized decompiler registers v8/v11; the intended node arguments are inferred, and whether this[v4] buckets and the two chain levels are distinct or overlapping is not established.
QuadPointerFree appears only as a name in the raw text of ResetAndFreeMemberArrays with no address evidence, so the trailing four-pointer block teardown target cannot be referenced.

Element types of the four counted arrays (580-, 48-, 48- and 72-byte strides) are not identified; the prelabel template's ctor_init categorization contradicts the observed teardown body and is treated as a false lead.
